chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who secretly married a woman from among his family, while she remained in the house of her family. He wanted to divorce her, but he could not reach her so as to know her menstruation when she menstruates, nor know her purity when she becomes pure.
So he said: “This is like one who is absent from his wife, so he divorces her according to lunar crescents and months.”
He said: I said, “What do you think if he can reach her at times and at other times cannot reach her, and so knows her condition—how should he divorce her?”

He said: “If a month passes for her while he cannot reach her, then he divorces her when he sees the first part of the next month, with witnesses, and he records the month in which he divorces her, and he has two men bear witness to her divorce. Then when three months have passed, she has become separated from him, and he is a suitor among the suitors; and her maintenance is upon him during those three months in which she observes her waiting period.”

key_terms.الْأَهِلَّةِ: lunar crescents; markers of the beginning of months
key_terms.بِطَمْثِهَا: her menstruation; the onset or state of menses relevant to divorce rulings
key_terms.بِطُهْرِهَا: her purity; the state of being free from menstruation
key_terms.خَاطِبٌ: a suitor; one eligible to seek marriage after separation
key_terms.سِرّاً: secretly; without public knowledge among the family
key_terms.نَفَقَتُهَا: her maintenance; financial support owed to her

ai.seo_question: How is a woman divorced in Shia fiqh if the husband cannot determine her menstruation or purity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on how a man may issue divorce when he cannot reliably know his wife's menstrual and purity state because she is inaccessible. The Imam عليه السلام treats such a case like that of an absent husband, tying the procedure to lunar months, witnesses, and the woman's waiting period, while affirming her maintenance during the ʿiddah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4807 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who secretly married a woman without his family knowing while she remained in her family's house. He wanted to divorce her but could not reach her to know when she menstruates or when she becomes pure.
Imam (as) said: "This is like a man who is absent from his wife, so he should divorce her based on lunar months and months."
I asked: "What if he sometimes has access to her and sometimes does not, so he knows her condition? How should he divorce her then?"
Imam (as) replied: "If a month passes without him reaching her, he should divorce her at the beginning of the next month with witnesses, writing down the month in which he divorces her and bringing two witnesses to testify to the divorce. Once three months have passed, she is completely separated from him, and he becomes like any other suitor. However, he must provide for her during those three months in which she observes her waiting period."
